dialog.body: {name} needs {count, plural, one {# Python package} other {# Python packages}} before it can run. Preparing builds its environment with {installer, select, uv {uv} pip {pip} other {the configured installer}} and downloads them from the package index.
dialog.bodyLocked: {name} pins {count, plural, one {# Python package} other {# Python packages}} in its uv.lock. Preparing installs exactly those versions with uv into its own environment, {offline, select, true {from the wheels it bundles} other {downloading them from the package index}}.
dialog.impact: This uses the network and disk space. Progress streams into the plugin's Logs tab, and you can keep working meanwhile.
dialog.impactOffline: This uses disk space; the plugin's packages are not downloaded. Progress streams into the plugin's Logs tab, and you can keep working meanwhile.
dialog.needsUv: uv is not installed, and only uv installs a uv.lock exactly. Cognia installs it first with the Python runtime's pip, which downloads it from the package index.
dialog.title: Prepare Python dependencies for {name}?

failedCause.lockOutOfDate: Its uv.lock no longer matches its pyproject.toml, so uv refused to install from it. The plugin's author needs to run uv lock and publish it again.
failedCause.missingWheels: It installs offline from the wheels it bundles, which lack {packages}. Nothing was downloaded.

state.needsUv: It is locked with uv.lock, which only uv installs exactly, and uv is not installed. Install uv to prepare it.
state.notPrepared: Its Python dependencies are not installed yet. Preparing them uses {installer}.
state.preparing: Its Python environment is being prepared with {installer}.
state.ready: Its {scope, select, shared {shared} isolated {isolated} other {}} Python environment matches what it declares (built with {installer}).
state.stale: Its Python environment no longer matches: {reasons}. Prepare it again before it runs.

staleReason.interpreter: it was built on another Python

userManaged.customInstaller: A custom installer builds its environment, so the host does not check it.
userManaged.interpreterOverride: It runs on the interpreter you chose, which the host does not prepare.
userManaged.venvDisabled: The managed environment is turned off; it runs on the Python you set up.

toast.failed: Couldn't prepare the Python dependencies of {name}
